PROTOCOLS

From this week’s stories, seven skills to try.

PUT YOUR JUDGMENT TO WORK

From “What’s Left for Humans After Automation” https://every.?ev_audience=free

 * Turn your corrections into checks. Mike pastes in an AI output for a task he repeats, says what he likes and doesn’t, and has the AI turn each comment into a yes-or-no check it can grade future outputs against. The prompt https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Ask an agent what your client needs next. Ode engineer Hugh Wimberly is helping an accounting firm use agents to find opportunities in its clients’ records. Give an agent the reports, meeting notes, and emails on the client, boss, or team you know best and ask what problem or opportunity they’re likely to face soon that they haven’t asked you about. The prompt https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Hire for tolerance of uncertainty. Nursa founder and CEO Curtis Anderson starts every interview process by asking candidates for examples of ambiguous situations they survived or grew through, at work or anywhere else. The questions https://every.?ev_audience=free

MAKE AI STUDY YOUR OWN TRACK RECORD

From “Your Attention Is AI’s New Bottleneck” https://every.?ev_audience=free

 * Find and fix where your coding agents get stuck. Product leader Trevin Chow https://every.?ev_audience=free built /ce-retro, which reads your past sessions in Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor, spots what your repo keeps making agents look up or relearn, and proposes fixes so the next session saves you time and tokens. Nothing changes until you approve. The skill https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Answer one question, not 30. In the formula Dan and Mike wrote, a question from an AI is worth asking only if you’ll actually answer it and your answer teaches the AI something. Next time you’re correcting an AI’s drafts, ask it to name one pattern in your edits and one exception it can’t explain. Explain only that exception. The formula https://every.?ev_audience=free

SIMULATE BEFORE YOU COMMIT

From Mike Taylor https://every.?ev_audience=free’s “The Next Two Levels of AI Adoption” https://every.?ev_audience=free

 * Make agent teams compete on strategy. Mike suggests having synthetic marketing teams each plan a product launch, pitch their plans to 50 synthetic customers built from interview transcripts, and revise over three rounds. The prompt https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Find out which wins were luck. He runs the same launch simulation 50 times, changing which launch orders and early reactions each customer sees, to determine which headline wins reliably and which only wins after a lucky start. The prompt https://every.?ev_audience=free

VIBE CHECKS

“Vibe Check: Fable 5.2 Is a Paradigm Shift—If You Know What to Do With It” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free/Vibe Check https://every.?ev_audience=free: Anthropic’s newest model earned gold, our top rating, from six of our seven testers. It’s the best we’ve used for long, ambitious builds like Kieran Klaassen https://every.?ev_audience=free’s video editor Everycut, but it’s slow and expensive, and Opus 5.5 https://every.?ev_audience=free still wins for everyday writing. Don’t jump to max effort: Senior director of consulting Ryan Wright found high beat max on anything that needed taste, and Kieran starts coding tasks at low.

“Vibe Check: Gemini 4 Carbon’s Coding Outpaces Its Judgment” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free/Vibe Check https://every.?ev_audience=free: Google DeepMind’s newest model is a much stronger coder than Gemini 4 Argon https://every.?ev_audience=free, and it doesn’t know when to stop. Told to take only the clearest tickets in a backlog, it ran for more than four hours until Mike stopped it. Give it one big job with a clear finish line, start at low thinking (it beat medium and high on Mike’s timed tasks), and check what it touched when it’s done.

KNOWLEDGE BASE

🎧 🖥 “What’s Left for Humans After Automation” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Grant Harvey https://every.?ev_audience=free/Context Window https://every.?ev_audience=free: In his Thesis: 2027 closing keynote, Dan says there are two ways to predict the future of work. The aggregate draws trend lines from benchmark data and makes AI look set to replace us, while the intimate looks closely at one situation and shows people improving alongside the models. Dan also explains why picking the right idea still takes a human: When the team ran one customer survey through Claude, go-to-market engineer Yash Poojary https://every.?ev_audience=free found new subscribers churning over too much email, and head of marketing Douglas Brundage https://every.?ev_audience=free found readers feeling isolated in their enthusiasm for AI. 🎧 🖥 Hear the full keynote on The Every Podcast: Listen on Spotify https://every.?ev_audience=free or Apple Podcasts https://every.?ev_audience=free, watch on X https://every.?ev_audience=free or YouTube https://every.?ev_audience=free, or read the transcript https://every.?ev_audience=free.

“The Next Two Levels of AI Adoption” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Mike Taylor https://every.?ev_audience=free/Also True for Humans https://every.?ev_audience=free: Users climbed our eight levels of AI adoption faster than Mike expected, so he added two more. At Level 9, Simulation, you set the goal, the scoring, and the rules, then let competing agent teams find the best plan. At Level 10, Multiverse, you rerun that competition many times to separate good strategies from lucky ones, which Mike learned when one extra early upvote sent identical posts down completely different paths in his Hacker News simulator.

“Your Attention Is AI’s New Bottleneck” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Grant Harvey https://every.?ev_audience=free/Context Window https://every.?ev_audience=free: Every’s Frontier team published what Dan calls the most important formula in AI, which measures how much a model learns about your taste per unit of your attention. The goal is creating a collaborator that makes you better just by talking to you. Plus: Why teams will keep paying for software anyone can vibe code, the pro video editor Kieran built in three days with Fable 5.2, a bad week for Nvidia, and the engineering job that’s up 4.6x as specialist roles shrink.

SIGNAL

WHY YOUR NEXT MODEL MIGHT BE MADE TO ORDER

What happened: This week, AI lab Goodfire showed https://every.?ev_audience=free that most “neurons” in an open-weight model do one or a few legible jobs, and AI agents can now predict when they fire with 95 percent accuracy. The new report backs up “Neural Networks Are Already Clean,” https://every.?ev_audience=free an October essay by Goodfire’s Nick Cammarata. One example: A neuron firing on both cat faces and car fronts, long cited as proof models are a mess, turns out to detect the V shape both have.

Separately, MIT researchers https://every.?ev_audience=free showed a frontier model can rewrite a smaller model’s weights without a training run. Last Friday, Cmpnd CEO (and Thesis Statement contributor https://every.?ev_audience=free) Drew Breunig released a Mac tool https://every.?ev_audience=free for this “weight-space programming”: $5 to $10 in GPT-6-Astra https://every.?ev_audience=free usage per model improved every small decision-making model his team tested.

Why it matters: Until now, we’ve all used the same models and gotten roughly the same answers. As Dan argued at Thesis https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIEFnZSBvZiBBcnRpc2FuYWwgQUkgSXMgQ29taW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDYxOSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vdHY_?ev_audience=free, that makes the default answer cheap and your perspective scarce, but models only get your point of view if you keep reminding them with style guides, memory files, and repasted prompts. If we can read models and start editing them, that could change.

What it means: Artisanal models are coming: designed around your taste rather than grown in a lab from data. Your saved corrections could become training data, and fine-tuning your own model could feel as easy as vibe coding a website.

This is all still early: Goodfire studied only one open model family, and Cmpnd’s prototype is likely a year or two from the mainstream.

Go deeper: Monologue https://every.?ev_audience=free, Every’s dictation app, runs on a laptop-sized model its two-person team trained to replace a roughly 1-trillion-parameter one: three times faster, fewer mistakes, far cheaper. In a Thesis talk, Monologue general manager Naveen Naidu https://every.?ev_audience=free covers when to train your own model, how to collect data, and how to ship almost daily. Watch How to Fine-tune Your Own Model https://every.to/emails/click/136f006095268802530f927779a5f4d55a493840c0f1f77c950761a77b64df9e/eyJzdWJqZWN0IjoiVGhlIEFnZSBvZiBBcnRpc2FuYWwgQUkgSXMgQ29taW5nIiwicG9zdF9pZCI6NDYxOSwicG9zdF90eXBlIjoicG9zdCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vZXZlcnkudG8vdHY_?ev_audience=free with a paid subscription https://every.?ev_audience=free.
